title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Bournemouth: Unlikely Hero Shines in Goal Fest
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott12:15 PM EDTChelsea were relentless. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesChelsea got back to winning ways in style on Saturday with an emphatic 5–1 victory over strugglers Bournemouth.

The hot starts returned to Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fans were still celebrating Jordan Henderson’s long-range opener when Morgan Rogers’s deflected effort nestled in the bottom corner to put Chelsea 2–0 ahead after two-and-a-half minutes.
Not content with the speed of their start in the first half, Chelsea were celebrating just 30 seconds after the restart when Pedro Neto’s cutback was rifled into the roof of the net by João Pedro.

Evanilson deflected Moisés Caicedo’s clearance into the back of the net five minutes later as the tone of the match changed drastically, so there was significant relief around Stamford Bridge when Pedro crashed home his second of the afternoon from close range.
The excellent Henderson’s stunning free kick iced the game off with 20 minutes to go, capping off a glorious afternoon for the veteran midfielder and sealing a much-needed victory for the Blues.

Defending continues to be a major problem for Chelsea. / Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesChelsea got their attacking mojo back here. The Blues were sensational, deserved each of their goals and could have had a few more if things had fallen another way.
This team can go toe-to-toe with any attack on the planet, but at the other end of the field, things are not the same.

The frailties that have plagued Chelsea for the past 18 months remain problematic. Defending set pieces is a massive concern and the sight of Evanilson celebrating the death of Emiliano Martínez’s clean sheet from a corner will be a lingering memory from this game.
Since the start of last season, Chelsea have now conceded a total of 14 goals from inside their own six-yard box following set pieces. Unsurprisingly, that is a league-high.

It is not a Xabi Alonso problem, considering how big of an issue this was under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior as well, but it is the former midfielder’s responsibility to figure out a solution. Until fixed, it will continue to provide any opponent a route back into a match regardless of the circumstances.
The attack is better than it has been in years. Now, it’s the turn of the defense.
Jordan Henderson stole the show for Chelsea. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Emiliano Martínez—7.7: A bystander for the most part before being called into action with an excellent double save in the 35th minute. Could do nothing for Evanilson’s strike.

CB: Josh Acheampong—7.4: Excellent on the ball, with a decisive role in Chelsea’s third goal, but needs to eradicate the defensive concerns that were on show for Evanilson’s goal. Overall, a good showing.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—7.1: Seemed a little off here, but didn’t really do anything wrong. Chelsea need more composure from the senior figure at the heart of their backline.

CB: Levi Colwill—7.1: Like Lacroix, Colwill was objectively fine, but a handful of nervy moments ensured his mixed start to the season continued here. It feels like we’re still waiting for the real Colwill to return from his ACL injury.
RM: Pedro Neto—8.0: Lacked a bit of energy in the first half but quickly made up for that with an impressive assist for the third goal.
CM: Moisés Caicedo—7.4: Made an immediate impact on his return to the squad, with his defensive instincts predictably valuable.

CM: Jordan Henderson—9.2: A really impressive showing. Took his early goal well, got the assist for Rogers, bagged a glorious free kick and led by example with his energy and passion. Such a strong performance.
